data.narrative:
Anduril Industries, a Series H defense and security company founded by Palmer Luckey, Brian Schimpf, Trae Stephens, Matt Grimm, and Joe Chen, is currently valued at $61B following $11B+ in cumulative fundraising. The Defense & Security sector contains 22 identifiable peers, though the private frontier-tech subsegment remains sparse: 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers including Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, Quantum-Systems, and Flock Safety.

A peer-median valuation approach is not applicable here. The narrow filters required for methodological rigor—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers—yielded fewer than three datapoints. Applying an all-sector median across the broader 22-company Defense & Security universe would introduce material distortion, as most peers operate at substantially different scales and stages than a $61B Series H entity. This constraint reflects the structural reality that few private frontier-tech defense firms have reached comparable scale or funding density.

The absence of a robust peer set means traditional triangulation cannot anchor a valuation range. The $61B current valuation reflects market consensus among sophisticated institutional investors (Series H participants), but external validation through comparable company analysis is unavailable. Key uncertainties include the durability of defense and security AI valuations amid shifting geopolitical demand, execution risk on customer concentration, and regulatory/export control changes. Any alternative valuation framework would require non-comparable-company methods or forward-looking cash flow assumptions not provided in this dataset.
